conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to ask you a few questions about your child.

**First question: How old is your child?**

Please tell me if your child is:
- Under 16 years old
- Between 16 and 19 years old
- 20 years old or over

This is important because eligibility rules differ depending on the child's age. Children under 16 automatically qualify (subject to other conditions), while 16-19 year olds need to be in approved education or training to qualify. Children 20 or over generally don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. My child Alex is 16 years old, so between 16 and 19.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16 years old (between 16 and 19), we need to check some additional requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex currently in education or training?**

Please tell me which of the following applies to Alex:

1. **Currently in education or training** - Alex is enrolled in and attending an approved course
2. **Recently left education** - Alex was in education but has left within the last few months
3. **Neither** - Alex is not in education/training and hasn't recently left

This is important because for 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit eligibility depends on being in approved education or training, or being within a specific extension period after leaving education.

Which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently left education. They finished school but have been working with the local careers service to figure out what to do next.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex recently left education, there may be an extension period during which you can still claim Child Benefit while Alex figures out their next steps.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! This is relevant to Alex's situation. There's a **20-week extension period** available for young people aged 16-17 who have recently left education.

**Important question: When did Alex leave education?**

To qualify for this extension period, Alex must have:
1. Left approved education or training **within the last 20 weeks**, AND
2. Registered with a qualifying service (which includes government careers services, Connexions, or the armed services)

You mentioned Alex has been working with the local careers service, which is good! 

**Can you tell me:**
- How many weeks ago did Alex finish school?
- Has Alex officially registered with the careers service (not just informally meeting with them)?

This will help me determine if Alex is still within the 20-week extension period.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex left school about 3 months ago, so that would be around 12 weeks. And yes, they've officially registered with the careers service - they had to sign up properly to get the appointments and support.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's helpful information. Since Alex left school about 12 weeks ago (which is within the 20-week extension period) and has officially registered with the careers service, Alex meets the requirements for the extension period.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

For Child Benefit eligibility, young people aged 16 and over cannot be working 24 hours or more per week (unless they're also in approved education or training).

Does Alex work:
- **Less than 24 hours per week** (or not working at all)?
- **24 hours or more per week**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't working at all right now. They're just focusing on sorting out what they want to do next with the careers service.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex isn't working, that meets this requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about benefits.

**Next question: Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to know if Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in their own name

Is Alex **NOT** receiving any of these benefits? (In other words, is Alex free from claiming these benefits in their own right?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't receiving any benefits in their own name. They don't claim anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's another requirement met.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good progress! Now I need to check about apprenticeships.

**Next question: Is Alex enrolled in any type of apprenticeship?**

This is important because different types of apprenticeships have different rules:
- **English apprenticeships** (all types) disqualify from Child Benefit
- **Scottish Modern Apprenticeships** disqualify
- **Welsh Foundation Apprenticeships** are approved and don't disqualify
- **Other Welsh apprenticeships** disqualify

So, is Alex:
- **Not in any apprenticeship** at all?
- **In an apprenticeship** (if so, which type and where)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. As I mentioned, they just left school and are working with the careers service to figure out their next steps.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, that's fine.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check your residency status, as you (the claimant) must meet UK residency requirements.

**Question about your residency: Do you normally live in the UK?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and meet certain conditions (working, studying, job seeking, or have sufficient resources)
4. You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation? Do you normally live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify as responsible if ANY of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common situation)
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards their care, such as food, clothes, pocket money, housing, or presents
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement that equals or exceeds the Child Benefit payment

Which applies to your situation? Do you live with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex lives with you, you meet the responsibility requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other claimants.

**Question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Any other person

Please tell me:
- **No one else is claiming** for Alex
- **Someone else is claiming** but they've agreed to transfer it to you
- **Someone else is claiming** and there's a dispute about who should claim

Which situation applies?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's good to know.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Question: Which of these best describes Alex's current living situation?**

- **Living normally at home** with you (no special circumstances)
- **In hospital** for medical care
- **In local authority care** (looked after by the council)
- **Fostered** by someone else

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me - no special circumstances.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is living normally at home with you, that's straightforward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final check.

**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying for any of Alex's living costs or upkeep? 

(Most families living normally at home would answer "no, the council isn't paying" - which means you'd meet this requirement.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - no, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. We're just a normal family living at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Since the council is not paying towards Alex's costs, you meet all the requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex!

### Why You're Eligible:

Alex qualifies under the **20-week extension period** for 16-17 year olds who have recently left education. Specifically:

- ✅ Alex is 16 years old (within the 16-19 age range)
- ✅ Alex left education about 12 weeks ago (within the 20-week extension period)
- ✅ Alex has officially registered with the government careers service
- ✅ Alex is not working (meets the under 24 hours/week requirement)
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own right
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for them
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ The council is not paying towards Alex's costs

### Important to Note:

The 20-week extension will continue **until the earlier of**:
- 20 weeks from when Alex left education (you're currently at week 12, so you have about 8 weeks remaining), OR
- When Alex turns 18

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** if you or your partner earns over £60,000
5. **Payments are made every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Apply Here:
👉 https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

If Alex starts education, training, or an approved course within this extension period, your eligibility may continue beyond the 20 weeks. Feel free to reach out if Alex's circumstances change!
